rationale: Thresholds and experiment design are fixed here before any result run of experiment v2. Nothing in this file may be edited in response to a measurement. A run that misses a threshold is a negative result and is reported as one.

v1.outcome: The completion gate exited 1. Both positive runs passed every threshold and can-corrupt and sensor-freeze were caught, but the cpu-hog control was never caught by its own contention: 22 spinning threads at the same scheduling policy as the control thread produced 0 missed deadlines and a p99 of 30 us against a frozen threshold of 1000 us, while burning 7.99 CPU-seconds in a 1.6 second window. sensor-freeze was caught, but on a knife edge of its own frozen bound: reaction times of 3, 9988, 9999 and 10004 us were measured against a 10000 us bound, so the same design would have failed the bound on a run whose boundary cycle jittered the other way.
v1.immutability: The v1 file is kept byte for byte and a test asserts its hash from both sides, so every v1 number stays checkable against the definition that produced it.

changes_from_v1.scope_statement: Exactly two changes. Nothing else about the experiment moves, and in particular no positive-gate threshold moves in either direction.

A_cpu_hog_is_a_strictly_higher_priority_.what_v1_did: The cpu-hog control ran its 2 x logical-core-count spinners at the same Mach THREAD_TIME_CONSTRAINT_POLICY the control thread had been granted. Peers at the same policy were chosen deliberately, and they never disturbed the loop: 0 missed deadlines, p99 30 us, peak jitter 1070 us.
A_cpu_hog_is_a_strictly_higher_priority_.what_v2_does: In the cpu-hog control run only, the control task does not request the time-constraint policy and runs at the default timeshare policy, while the 2 x logical-core-count hog threads request the Mach time-constraint policy. Positive runs are unchanged: they request the time-constraint policy exactly as v1 did.
A_cpu_hog_is_a_strictly_higher_priority_.why: The brief asks for a 'higher-priority' CPU hog. v1's hog was a same-priority hog, which is a different and weaker experiment: it can only ever show that peers at equal priority do not preempt each other. On this host the Mach time-constraint band is the highest scheduling band a user process can request, so the only way to make the hog strictly higher priority than the control task is to leave the control task in the band below it for the duration of that one control run.
A_cpu_hog_is_a_strictly_higher_priority_.second_lever_not_used: pthread_set_qos_class_self_np was explored as a second lever and is not used. See design_exploration: QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE on the hog changed nothing measurable, and QOS_CLASS_BACKGROUND on the control thread destroyed the loop everywhere in the run rather than inside the hog window, which would have made attribution impossible.
A_cpu_hog_is_a_strictly_higher_priority_.what_stays_the_same: Thread count (2 x logical cores), the window (the middle 40 percent of the run), the spin body, spawning before the timed loop and joining after it, and the caught criterion.

B_watchdog_timeout_is_eight_periods.what_v1_did: The staleness budget was 100000 us, ten periods, and the sensor-freeze control required the trip to land within 10000 us (one period) of the budget expiring. Measured reactions were 3, 9988, 9999 and 10004 us against that 10000 us bound.
B_watchdog_timeout_is_eight_periods.what_v2_does: The staleness budget is 80000 us, eight periods. The sensor-freeze criterion becomes: the safe state must be entered within 100000 us of the timestamp of the last accepted sensor frame.
B_watchdog_timeout_is_eight_periods.why: The brief asks for a 'watchdog safe state within 100 ms'. v1 read that as a 100 ms budget plus a one-period reaction bound, which makes the requirement a knife edge: the check runs once per period, so the reaction is one period plus the difference between two jitter samples, and the boundary cycle either trips or lands just over the bound. Reading the brief literally instead, 100 ms is the bound on the whole path from the last good reading to the safe state. An 80 ms budget checked once per 10 ms period enters the safe state about 90 ms after the last accepted frame, which satisfies the literal requirement with about one period of margin rather than by luck.
B_watchdog_timeout_is_eight_periods.what_stays_the_same: The watchdog is still fed only by accepted frames, still latches, still commands the safe actuator value, and the positive gate still requires that it never trips on a positive run.

positive_gate_unchanged_statement: The positive_gate block below is byte-identical to the positive_gate block of manifest/frozen-v1.json. Every threshold, every definition and every wording is the same: missed_deadlines_max 0, p99_jitter_us_max 1000, rejected_frames_max 0, watchdog_may_trip false, over 10000 cycles at a 10000 us period with seed 20260909. Neither change above weakens or strengthens it.

execution_environment.bus: simulated, deterministic, in-process; no physical CAN transceiver and no CAN adapter is attached to the machine
execution_environment.sensor: simulated first-order plant driven by the node's own actuator command; no physical sensor
execution_environment.microcontroller_status: cross-compile check only: fieldbus-core builds for thumbv7em-none-eabihf and has never been flashed or executed on a device
execution_environment.scheduling: POSIX-hosted periodic loop with deadline telemetry. On a positive run the Mach time-constraint policy is requested as a best effort and the grant result is recorded, not assumed. On the cpu-hog control run the control thread deliberately does not request it; see changes_from_v1.A.
execution_environment.socketcan_status: The SocketCAN backend is type-checked locally by cross-compiling and executed only in CI, against a kernel loopback vcan0 that the workflow creates. A virtual interface is not a bus and is not hardware in the loop.
execution_environment.hil_json_rationale: No physical hardware is available on this machine, so results/hil.json is deliberately not produced. Its absence is the honest outcome, not a gap to be filled with a simulator run relabelled.
execution_environment.machine_is_not_quiet: Other processes, including a long-running training job, were on this machine while v2 was frozen and run. That is stated rather than controlled for: a positive run that only passes on an idle laptop is not a result worth reporting, and a control that only fires on a busy one is not either.

loop.seed_rationale: A single fixed seed drives the simulated plant's measurement noise. The fault injector schedule is by explicit cycle index, not by the seed, so an injected fault lands at the same cycle regardless of seed.

watchdog.timeout_rationale: Eight periods, so that a watchdog evaluated once per 10000 us period enters the safe state about 90000 us after the last accepted sensor frame and satisfies the literal 100000 us requirement with roughly one period of margin. The host reads this value from this file and constructs the node's watchdog with it, so the budget cannot drift from the frozen experiment.

positive_gate.description: All four conditions must hold on both positive runs for the completion gate to pass.
positive_gate.deadline_miss_definition: A cycle whose work finishes later than its own scheduled start plus one period. Every period that passes with no cycle executing in it at all is counted as a miss as well, so lateness cannot be hidden by simply running fewer cycles than periods elapsed.
positive_gate.jitter_definition: Actual cycle start minus scheduled cycle start, in microseconds, where scheduled start is t0 + i * period computed once from the monotonic clock so error does not accumulate. Early wakes are recorded as zero.
positive_gate.p99_reporting: Upper edge of the 10 us histogram bucket containing the nearest-rank p99 sample, so the reported figure is never optimistic.

negative_controls.mechanism: During the middle 40 percent of the run (cycles 3000 through 6999 of 10000), 2 x logical-core-count threads that requested the Mach time-constraint policy spin, while the control task runs at the default timeshare policy for the whole of this run. The spinners are created before the timed loop and joined after it; inside the loop they are only switched on and off, which is a lock, a store and a notify.
negative_controls.priority_relation_required: The hog threads must be in a strictly higher scheduling band than the control task. The run's result file records what each side requested, what the kernel granted, and the QoS class each side ended up in, so a reader can check the relation held rather than assume it.
negative_controls.expected: The positive gate is violated: missed_deadlines > 0 OR p99 jitter > 1000 us.
negative_controls.caught_definition: caught == true if and only if the positive gate fails on this run. This is unchanged from v1.
negative_controls.attribution_reporting: The run's own uncontended head (cycles 0 through 2999) and tail (cycles 7000 through 9999) are the within-run baseline: same demoted control thread, no hog. The result file reports missed deadlines and jitter percentiles inside the hog window and outside it separately, and every miss keeps its cycle index, so the hog's contribution is separable from the demotion's.
negative_controls.attribution_expected_before_the_run: Frozen here so it cannot be written after seeing the numbers. Exploration measured a demoted control thread with no hog at all at p50 2001 us and p99 2507 us with 0 missed deadlines, and the same thread with the hog running at an in-window p99 of about 20000 us with every missed deadline inside the window. So: the p99 condition is expected to fail even outside the hog window and is NOT by itself attributable to the hog, while missed deadlines and the in-window jitter excess are. If this run is caught with zero missed deadlines and an out-of-window p99 already above 1000 us, the honest reading is that the gate caught the demotion and not the contention, and it is to be reported that way.
negative_controls.if_not_caught: Report the control as NOT caught and say so. The gate is not to be weakened to make it catch.

negative_controls.mechanism: At the fixed cycles listed below, inject one additional malformed frame alongside the valid one for that cycle. Injecting an extra frame rather than corrupting the in-stream frame is deliberate: it keeps the legitimate sequence intact so each injected fault produces exactly one rejection attributable to exactly one reason, with no cascade into the next cycle.
negative_controls.expected: Every injected frame is rejected under its intended reason, no legitimate frame is rejected, and the positive gate's rejected == 0 condition therefore fails.
negative_controls.caught_definition: caught == true if and only if rejected == 20 AND the per-reason histogram matches expected_rejected_by_reason exactly AND accepted == expected_accepted AND the positive gate fails on this run.

negative_controls.mechanism: The simulated sensor stops emitting at cycle 5000 and never resumes.
negative_controls.expected: The watchdog enters the safe state within 100000 us of the last accepted sensor frame, the SensorStale reason persists to the end of the run, the actuator command is 0 from the trip onward, and the positive gate's watchdog condition therefore fails.
negative_controls.reaction_time_definition: tripped_at_us - last_seen_us, where last_seen_us is the timestamp of the last accepted sensor frame and tripped_at_us is the timestamp of the check that latched the safe state. This is the whole path the brief bounds at 100 ms, not the overshoot past the internal budget that v1 measured.
negative_controls.nominal_caveat: Nominal values assume an ideal clock. The check runs at each cycle's actual wake time, so wake jitter can move the trip by one cycle in either direction; the 10000 us nominal margin exists so that it does not matter. Only max_reaction_time_us is a criterion; the nominal values are recorded so a reader can see the design intent and a surprise is visible as a surprise.
negative_controls.caught_definition: caught == true if and only if the watchdog tripped AND its reason is sensor_stale AND reaction_time_us <= 100000 AND the actuator command is 0 for every cycle from the trip to the end AND the safe state is still latched at the end of the run AND the positive gate fails on this run.

design_exploration.what_this_is: Short runs made BEFORE this manifest was frozen, to find out whether any available mechanism can make a strictly higher-priority hog disturb this loop on this host, and to check that the mechanism chosen is the one doing the disturbing. Run with a standalone probe outside the repository that replicates the runner's sleep-to-absolute-target loop and the hog's condvar-gated spinners, at a 10000 us period with 22 spinners on 11 logical cores, hog window the middle 40 percent. Outputs kept under .agent-work/, which is never committed. These are not results of the experiment; they are what the experiment was designed against.
design_exploration.host: Apple M3 Pro, 11 logical cores (6 performance, 5 efficiency), macOS, with a long-running training job on the machine throughout.

runs.result: p50 6 us, p99 20 us, max 98 us, 0 missed deadlines.
runs.reading: The elevated control thread is clean on a loaded machine. This is the regime the positive runs use and it is unchanged in v2.

runs.result: in-window p99 10 us, out-of-window p99 28 us, max 49 us, 0 missed deadlines.
runs.reading: v1's null result reproduces in six seconds. The v1 hog is not weak, it is simply a peer: nothing about 22 spinning threads at the same policy reaches this loop.

runs.result: p50 2001 us, p99 2507 us, max 2697 us, 0 missed deadlines, and the same figures inside and outside the nominal window.
runs.reading: The confound, found before freezing and stated here because of it. Demoting the control thread out of the time-constraint band costs about 2 ms of wake latency by itself, uniformly, with no hog running at all. That alone exceeds the 1000 us p99 threshold. So in v2 a p99 violation on the cpu-hog run is NOT evidence of contention, while a missed deadline is: the demoted baseline misses none.

runs.result: in-window p99 20147 us against out-of-window p99 2498 us; max 29278 us; missed deadlines 16, 2 and 0 across the three runs, every one of them inside the hog window and none outside it.
runs.reading: The chosen mechanism. The hog moves in-window p99 by roughly an order of magnitude over the same thread's own out-of-window baseline in the same run, and every deadline miss lands inside the window. Miss counts vary run to run, which is why the frozen criterion stays the gate violation rather than a miss count.

runs.result: in-window p99 21276 us, out-of-window p99 2471 us, 10 missed deadlines, all inside the window. All 22 threads had both the policy and the QoS class granted.
runs.reading: The QoS lever on the hog side changes nothing measurable: the time-constraint band is already above every QoS band. Not used, so v2 makes exactly one scheduling call per side and the priority relation stays easy to state.

runs.result: p50 39796 us, p99 99364 us, 684 missed deadlines, of which 406 were OUTSIDE the hog window and 278 inside.
runs.reading: Rejected. Background QoS confines the thread to efficiency cores and wrecks the loop everywhere in the run, so more misses land outside the hog window than inside it. It would make the control fire loudly and prove nothing, which is the failure mode v1 already documented three times.

design_exploration.conclusion: Freeze E1's mechanism: control thread at the default timeshare policy for the cpu-hog run only, hog threads at the Mach time-constraint policy, no QoS calls on either side. Report the in-window and out-of-window figures separately in the result file, because on this host the demotion alone clears the p99 threshold and only the missed deadlines and the in-window excess are attributable to the contention.

completion_gate.pass_condition: Exit 0 if and only if both positive runs satisfy every condition in positive_gate AND all three negative controls report caught == true.
completion_gate.negative_control_safety: Each fault is reachable only through its own explicit CLI subcommand and is selected only by this script. No fault is enabled by default and none is committed in an on state. The cpu-hog control's demoted control-thread policy is part of that subcommand and of nothing else: a positive run requests the time-constraint policy exactly as it did in v1.
